12	ThAME: 3D Memory-Enabled Heterogeneous 
13	Accelerator for LLM Mixture of Experts 
14	 
15	Pratyush Dhingra, Graduate Student Member, IEEE, Pramit Kumar Pal, Graduate Student Member, IEEE,  
16	Janardhan Rao Doppa, Senior Member, IEEE, and Partha Pratim Pande, Fellow, IEEE 
17	 
18	 
19	   Abstract—Mixture of Experts (MoE) architectures have 
20	emerged as a dominant paradigm for scaling Large Language 
21	Models (LLMs) . However, MoE inference on conventional 
22	hardware is constrained by three fundamental bottlenecks. These 
23	encompass the massive memory bandwidth required to fetch non-
24	contiguous expert weights, the non -deterministic scatter -gather 
25	traffic generated by input -dependent token routing, and the tail -
26	latency dependency imposed by synchronous expert output 
27	aggregation. To address these challenges, we propose ThAME, a 
28	three-dimensional (3D) heterogeneous multi -chiplet architecture 
29	for MoE inference. ThAME employs Ferroelectric Field -Effect 
30	Transistor (FeFET)-based non-volatile and DRAM-based volatile 
31	memory chiplets with a co -designed compute mapping strategy 
32	that aligns the distinct computational profiles of attention 
33	mechanisms and expert routing . Furthermore, we design a 
34	specialized Network-on-Chip communication backbone optimized 
35	to mitigate the bottlenecks associated with non-deterministic token 
36	routing traffic across the combinatorial space of input -dependent 
37	MoE traffic patterns . Experimental results demonstrate that 
38	ThAME outperforms state-of-the-art counterparts by up to 15.7× 
39	in terms of speedup and improves energy efficiency by up to 9.8×. 
40	 
41	Index Terms —Mixture of Experts, Heterogeneous Architecture, 
42	Processing-Near-Memory, Network-on-Chip, 3D Integration.

44	I. INTRODUCTION 
45	arge Language Models (LLMs) have become a 
46	foundational paradigm in modern AI, delivering  state-
47	of-the-art performance across diverse applications 
48	including language, code, vision, and robotics [1]. Built on the 
49	transformer architecture, they leverage self -attention 
50	mechanisms to capture long -range dependencies  and achieve 
51	exceptional accuracy and generalization capabilities  [1].  
52	Recently, the Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture is rapidly 
53	 
54	 
55	 
56	becoming the preferred practical paradigm to efficiently scale 
57	these models to billions of parameters [2]. By activating a small 
58	subset of specialized experts per token, MoE -based LLMs 
59	achieve high representational power of dense feed -forward 
60	networks through sparse computation [2]. 
61	However, this sparse computation in MoE -based LLM 
62	inference poses significant challenges. First, MoE models 
63	demand enormous memory capacity to store the vast number of 
64	static expert weights. During the autoregressive decode phase, 
65	each generated token nece ssitates fetching large, non -
66	contiguous expert weight matrices from memory. This 
67	memory-bound nature saturates the available bandwidth on 
68	conventional computing platforms such as GPUs, leaving 
69	compute units underutilized [3], [4] . Second, the input -
70	dependent nature of MoE execution produces irregular 
71	dataflow.

92	V. EXPERIMENTAL RESULTS 
93	In this section, we first describe the experimental setup used 
94	for the performance evaluation  of ThAME. Next, we analyze 
95	the ThAME compute core design followed by the NoC design 
96	within the FeFET -NAND die . Afterwards, we analyze the 
97	effectiveness of both the computation and communication 
98	optimization during expert processing . We then present a 
99	sensitivity analysis under degraded FeFET read latency. 
100	Finally, we present a comparative and end -to-end analysis of 
101	ThAME against the baselines  in terms of performance and 
102	energy during MoE LLM inference. 
103	A. Experimental Setup 
104	We consider a diverse range of LLM models in our 
105	evaluation, as outlined in Table I . These models represent the 
106	typical size and diversity of real -world use  cases for 
107	deployment. A 16-bit fixed-point data representation was used 
108	as the precision of all model parameters and activations.  
109	Compute Modeling: We employed a cycle-accurate simulator 
110	to determine the latency and energy for each compute unit. 
111	SCALE-Sim was used to model the latency for each systolic 
112	array within the base die of memory chiplets and the host [34]. 
113	For the FeFET -NAND P NM chiplet, a modified version of 
114	NeuroSim was employed to capture the latency and energy of 
115	the 3D memory array [39]. NeuroSim has been validated against 
116	post-layout SPICE simulations of a taped -out PIM macro, 
117	showing chip-level prediction error below 1% after calibration 
118	for area, latency, and energy metrics. Similarly, SCALE-Sim has 
119	been verified against production TPU hardware with median 
120	relative error below 3% for representative operators [34]. Table 
121	II provides the detailed specifications of the FeFET -NAND, 
122	DRAM, and host chiplets used in our evaluation.  
123	Communication Modeling:  BookSim2, a cycle -accurate 
124	simulator, was used to model the  intra-chiplet NoC [40]. The 
125	inputs to the BookSim2 are the connectivity between routers, the 
126	intra-chiplet traffic, the link bandwidth, and the routing 
127	algorithm. Table III shows the NoC parameters for modeling the 
128	inter-core links within the FeFET-NAND chiplet.  
129	In this work, we have implemented ThAME using a 
130	configuration with two FeFET and two DRAM memory chiplets 
131	along with a systolic array (TPU v6e) based host chiplet on a 
132	silicon interposer. Each of the memory chiplets is connected to 
133	the host chiplet in a point -to-point manner through the 
134	interposer. Note that this specific configuration does not affect 
135	the generalizability of our findings.  We compare ThAME 
136	against two heterogeneous accelerators, Stratum (a DRAM -
137	PNM and compute -centric host) and H3D -T (a 3D -stacked 
138	FeFET, SRAM, and TPU architecture)  [9], [15]. The base die 
139	area for both the DRAM and the FeFET -NAND chiplet is kept 
140	consistent at  121 mm 2, simi lar to the baseline Stratum for 
141	comparison. For H3D-T, we instantiat e multiple instances to 
142	establish an iso-area configuration for a fair evaluation. 
143	The base  die within the FeFET -NAND chiplet consists of 
144	systolic array-based computing cores. We follow existing work 
145	to determine the area and power for the memory peripherals, 
146	PHY and the power-delivery network for the base die [15]. To 
147	perform the thermal evaluation and to ensure the feasibility of 
148	the 3D-stacked base die without inducing thermal throttling, we 
149	employed HotSpot [41]. We performed a steady -state 
150	simulation at a 45 C ambient to establish an allowable budget of 
151	50W for the base die, using the parameters detailed in Table III. 
152	Given the area budget and FeFET memory bandwidth in our 
153	experimental setup, we provisioned a total of 4,096 PEs per core 
154	in a 32-core system under maximum utilization where all cores 
155	are simultaneously active. Table IV details the specifications of 
156	the systolic array  cores. We employ the Archived Multi -
157	Objective Simulated Annealing (AMOSA) algorithm to identify 
158	the Pareto-Optimal set of designs (𝒟∗) for our hierarchical NoC 
159	design. AMOSA is a simulated annealing-based MOO solver in 
160	which the optimization process is guided using an archive of 
161	previously explored solutions [38]. The design space exploration

200	In parallel, industry has begun exploring high -bandwidth 
201	NAND with near -memory compute for AI inference. SanDisk 
202	and SK Hynix have jointly defined the High -Bandwidth Flash 
203	(HBF) standard, which stacks NAND dies at HBM-comparable 
204	bandwidth with up to 512 GB  per stack [19], [20]. SK Hynix's 
205	H³ architecture integrates HBM and HBF on a shared interposer 
206	alongside a GPU, reporting up to 2.69× higher throughput per 
207	watt over HBM -only configurations for LLM inference [21]. 
208	While these efforts confirm the practical feasibility of dense 
209	NAND for overcoming DRAM's capacity and refresh 
210	limitations, they rely on conventional Flash, which imposes 
211	high access latency and energy overheads. Moreover, similar to 
212	existing HBM -based PNM systems, they provide no intra -
213	chiplet fabric to manage the irregular, scatter -gather data 
214	exchange among compute cores during MoE token routing. 
215	Collectively, these efforts advance either storage density or 
216	raw bandwidth, yet none couples low -latency, high -density 
217	storage with a communication fabric designed for MoE traffic. 
218	This gap motivates a co -designed architecture that integrates 
219	such storage with a specialized NoC to break both the memory 
220	and communication bottlenecks of MoE inference. 
221	III. PROBLEM STATEMENT 
222	Each layer within a transformer based LLM is composed of 
223	two computational modules: Multi-Head Attention (MHA) and 
224	Feed-Forward (FFN) [1]. While the MHA module remains 
225	consistent across LLMs and MoE models, the structure of the 
226	FFN is fundamentally different between these architectures . In 
227	MoE, the monolithic FFN of LLMs is replaced with a sparse 
228	layer of independent specialized experts (see Fig. 2)  [2], [17]. 
229	Specifically, a MoE layer consists of a Router (or Gating 
230	Network) and a set of 𝑁 independent expert networks 𝐸 =
231	 {𝐸1, … , 𝐸𝑁}, each implemented as a standard FFN, where 
232	computation is inherently sparse, activating only a small subset 
233	of relevant experts per input [2], [17]. 
234	For a given input token representation 𝑥, the gating network  
235	𝐺(𝑥) computes a sparse probability distribution, selecting only 
236	the top-𝑘 experts (where 𝑘 ≪ 𝑁) to process the token, as shown 
237	in Fig. 2 . Afterwards, the output 𝑦 is the weighted sum of the 
238	selected experts' outputs, as described in Eq. 1: 
239	                                  𝑦 =  ∑ 𝐺(𝑥)𝑖. 𝐸𝑖(𝑥)𝑖 ∈𝑇                          (1) 
240	where 𝑇 represents the set of indices corresponding to the 
241	top-𝑘 experts. While this sparsity keeps the number of active 
242	parameters per token comparable to a smaller model, the total 
243	number of model parameters to be stored for all experts can be 
244	orders of magnitude larger. This shift in neural architecture 
245	creates fundamental challenges : MoE models are 
246	computationally sparse but memory -dense, introducing 
247	significant irregularity in dataflow. The workload transitions 
248	from the uniform matrix multiplication  characteristic of LLMs 
249	to scattered, input-dependent conditional computation in MoEs, 
250	creating both computation and communication bottlenecks. 
251	First, t he expert weights dominate the model size (often >  
252	90%). Storing these massive parameters in off -chip Flash 
253	memory incurs prohibitive latency and energy penalties, while 
254	on-chip DRAM lacks the required density. Consequently, 
255	efficient expert computation demands a high -density storage 
256	medium capable of low-latency access. 
257	Second, the active experts are dynamically allocated to the 
258	computing cores. Considering a manycore architecture, the 
259	gating mechanism dictates the workload distribution for a batch 
260	of input tokens. This results in highly variable , non-
261	deterministic traffic patterns that change based on the semantic 
262	content of the batch [12]. Tokens must be dispatched to their 
263	assigned experts and output results aggregated, introducing 
264	significant network latency [13]. Furthermore, the aggregation 
265	of expert outputs imposes a synchronous aggregation operation, 
266	where the inference latency is dictated by the completion of the 
267	slowest expert.  
268	From a combinatorial perspective, the allocation of 𝑞 cores to 
269	𝑒 active experts can be modeled as partitioning the integer 𝑞 
270	into 𝑒 parts. Consequently, the total number of unique NoC 
271	traffic scenarios (𝑆), for a system with 𝑞 cores is given by the 
272	sum of partition functions, as expressed in Eq. 2: 
273	                                       𝑆 =  ∑ 𝑝𝑗(𝑞)
274	𝑒
275	𝑗=1                                   (2) 
276	Here, 𝑝𝑗(𝑞) represents the number of integer partitions of 𝑞 into 
277	exactly 𝑗 positive parts. 
278	This combinatorial explosion of traffic patterns , combined 
279	with the memory-bound nature of experts, impose the following 
280	design challenges unique to MoE-based LLM inference: 
281	1) Memory Bottleneck of Experts:  The expert layers 
282	require massive storage density and high bandwidth to 
283	feed compute units. Existing memory hierarchies fail to 
284	balance the trade-off between density, leakage, and access 
285	latency for these sparse, static weights.

351	VI. CONCLUSION 
352	MoE neural architectures have emerged as a powerful 
353	paradigm for scaling LLMs, but their deployment is 
354	fundamentally bottlenecked by the extreme memory demands 
355	of static expert weights and the non -deterministic 
356	communication traffic due to input -dependent expert routing. 
357	This paper presented ThAME, a three -dimensional 
358	heterogeneous architecture designed to accelerate MoE 
359	inference. By harnessing the high storage density of 3D FeFET-
360	NAND memory for experts, ThAME stores model parameters 
361	on-chip, effectively breaking the memory wall. Furthermor e, 
362	we design a customized hierarchical NoC for the intra -chiplet 
363	traffic within FeFET -NAND. This specialized communication 
364	backbone reduces link utilization variance, mitigating the 
365	multi-hop congestion and tail -latency stalls that cripple 
366	conventional topologies such as mesh during expert processing.

63	Abstract
64	Vision-language-action (VLA) models have emerged as a key com-
65	ponent in embodied AI. Among existing approaches, diffusion-
66	based VLA models achieve superior motion quality and generaliza-
67	tion. However, diffusion-based VLA models are compute-intensive
68	and must run at high control frequency, e.g., 50–200 Hz. Thus, it
69	imposes strict latency and energy constraints on edge devices.
70	In this work, we presentDeltoris 1, an algorithm–hardware
71	co-design framework for efficient diffusion-based VLA inference.
72	First, we exploit the temporal similarity of consecutive inputs and
73	propose atemporal-aware bit-sparsityalgorithm that computes only
74	the differences between consecutive inputs, eliminating redundant
75	bit-level operations. To further address the extra off-chip traffic
76	introduced by our algorithm, we propose aspeculative inference
77	technique, which amortizes data loading across multiple control
78	steps. Lastly, to support these techniques, we co-design a dedicated
79	accelerator with customized 1D systolic bit-serial PE arrays that
80	eliminate PE workload imbalance. Our evaluation shows thatDel-
81	torisachieves up to 34.2 × speedup over mobile GPUs and 6.1 ×
82	over prior accelerators, while maintaining comparable accuracy.

90	1 Introduction
91	Recent advances in embodied artificial intelligence (AI) have en-
92	abled robots to perform complex tasks in real-world environments [1,
93	32, 34, 104, 117]. At the core of these systems are vision-language-
94	action (VLA) models, which integrate visual perception, instruction
95	understanding, and action generation into a unified framework. By
96	leveraging multimodal inputs, VLA models allow robots to interpret
97	high-level instructions and convert them into control commands.

104	compression [8, 19, 35], sparse attention [15, 49, 94], etc. In con-
105	trast, VLA models remain largelyunder-exploredin the architecture
106	community. Currently, enabling VLA models on robotic platforms
107	in real-time is challenging due to their latency and energy con-
108	straints. Existing robotic platforms often fail to meet the real-time
109	requirements (50–200 Hz). For instance, a well-known VLA model,
110	PAD [26], can only execute at 2.0 Hz on a mobile Nvidia Orin
111	SoC (Fig. 2). Thus, this paper aims to enable real-time and energy-
112	efficient VLA model inference on robotic platforms.
113	Among the VLA models [5, 6, 12, 20, 26, 36, 43, 53, 54, 61, 90, 92,
114	96, 105] proposed in recent years, diffusion-based models [5, 12, 20,
115	26, 36, 53, 61, 90, 92] have emerged as a promising approach for
116	robot control. Compared to other inference paradigms, diffusion-
117	based VLA models can produce smooth motion trajectories and
118	achieve better generality among unseen environments by predicting
119	the action distribution through an iterative noise-denoising process.
120	Recent works, such as Diffusion Policy [12], UVA [36], VPP [36], and
121	Diffusion-VLA [90] demonstrate that diffusion-based approaches
122	can outperform traditional auto-regressive (AR) policies in many
123	robotic manipulation benchmarks. In this paper, we primarily focus
124	on diffusion-based VLA models.
125	Motivation.Despite their advantages, diffusion-based VLA
126	models are compute-intensive. They require tens of iterative de-
127	noising steps to generate one individual action, resulting in a higher
128	latency compared to their AR counterparts. Each denoising step
129	involves executing a deep neural network (DNN) to progressively
130	refine a noisy trajectory into a valid control signal. Our roofline anal-
131	ysis in Fig. 5 shows that existing diffusion-based VLA models are
132	compute-bound rather than memory-bound. Thus, it is important
133	to reduce the overall computation of diffusion-based VLA models.
134	To do so, our key insight is that consecutive robot observations,
135	e.g., poses and images, in robotic control loops exhibit extremely
136	high similarity, given the fact that robot control operates at a high
137	frequency. Our experiment in Fig. 7 shows that over 98% of pixels
138	between consecutive camera frames often remain unchanged due to
139	the small time interval between controls. As a result, a large portion
140	of the computation during VLA inference is redundant. Potentially,
141	we can enable orders-of-magnitude speedup for diffusion-based
142	VLA inference by exploiting this temporal redundancy.
143	Framework.To exploit this insight, we proposeDeltoris, an al-
144	gorithm–hardware co-design framework for accelerating diffusion-
145	based VLA models.Deltorisexploits the high temporal similarity
146	inherent in robotic control loops and introduces atemporal-aware
147	bit-level sparsityalgorithm that processes only the differences be-
148	tween consecutive inputs (Sec. 4). Similar to the execution of spiking
149	neural networks [98],Deltorisrepresents differential inputs in bi-
150	nary form and executes computations only on active “1” bits while
151	skipping redundant operations. Our experiment shows in Fig. 17
152	that we can achieve up to 92.9% operation reduction.
153	Although our bit sparsity algorithm significantly reduces arith-
154	metic operations, it introduces additional off-chip data traffic due to
155	the extra intermediate data loading. We show that a naive bit spar-
156	sity implementation can increase the off-chip data traffic by 1.8×.
157	We found that the VLA workloads essentially shift from compute-
158	bound to memory-bound after applying our bit-level sparsity al-
159	gorithm. To mitigate the DRAM traffic overhead, we propose a
160	technique calledspeculative inferencein Sec. 5, inspired by specula-
161	tive decoding in LLMs [50, 63]. In our approach, a lightweight VLA
162	model first speculatively predicts multiple future actions, while a
163	more accurate but compute-intensive VLA model validates these
164	predictions. To maintain robustness, no actions are actually applied
165	to the robots before being validated by the larger VLA model. In this
166	way, both model weights and intermediate data of the larger model
167	can be loaded only once when validating all predicted poses. Thus,
168	our approach amortizes data loading across multiple validation
169	steps, reducing off-chip data traffic.
170	Architecture.To fully unlock the potential ofDeltoris, we
171	design a dedicated accelerator tailored for diffusion-based VLA in-
172	ference in Sec. 6. The key contribution of our design is to eliminate
173	the workload imbalance commonly observed in bit-serial accel-
174	erators that exploit bit-level sparsity. Specifically, we employ an
175	output-stationary dataflow that shares activations across multi-
176	ple processing elements (PEs). We further introduce a novel 1D
177	systolic bit-serial PE array. Compared with prior bit-serial acceler-
178	ators, our proposed PE array largely simplifies control logic and
179	improves both performance and energy efficiency. Combined with
180	our co-designed encoding and decoding modules, our architecture
181	effectively reduces both on-chip and off-chip data movement.

19	Abstract—Developing high-performance kernels for Neu-
20	ral Processing Units (NPUs) is a critical industry bottle-
21	neck, requiring developers to manually navigate implicit
22	hardware constraints and strict memory hierarchies. While
23	large language models offer immense automation potential,
24	they fail catastrophically on NPUs due to a fundamental
25	lack of hardware-specific priors. Na ¨ıvely transplanting
26	code snippets from similar NPU kernels may pass the
27	compiler, but it consistently triggers runtime crashes and
28	performance degradation by blindly violating underlying
29	hardware constraints. To overcome this, we introduce
30	Hawk, a training-free framework that harnesses hardware-
31	aware knowledge through three core modules: (1) Run-
32	Time Knowledge Synthesis Module, which employs a
33	Triple-Part Executable Knowledge Representationto inher-
34	ently couple the error context with executable semantics;
35	(2) Bottleneck-Aware Knowledge Retrieval Module, which
36	implements a2D-Retrievalparadigm to project queries
37	into orthogonal syntactic and hardware-aligned seman-
38	tic spaces; and (3) Effect-Driven Knowledge Distillation
39	Module, which leveragesLLM-driven semantic arbitration
40	to continuously distill the knowledge by pruning errors
41	and consolidating redundancies based on the empirical
42	execution feedback. Extensive evaluations on real-world
43	NPU workloads demonstrate that Hawk elevates generation
44	accuracy from 49.4% to 80.0%, while achieving up to a
45	2.2×execution speedup over state-of-the-art baselines.
46	Index Terms—NPU, Kernel Generation, Harness Engi-
47	neering, Automatic Programming.
48	I. INTRODUCTION
49	Domain-specific accelerators like Neural Processing
50	Units (NPUs) are critical for modern AI workloads, yet
51	automating NPU kernel generation via Large Language
52	Models (LLMs) [1]–[4] remains notoriously difficult.
53	Our empirical study (§III) shows state-of-the-art LLMs
54	achieve merely 13.3% Comp@1 (compilation success
55	rate) and 13.3% Pass@1 (functional correctness rate) on
56	NPUs, starkly contrasting with GPU generation (100%
57	Comp@1, 80% Pass@1). We find that over 75% of
58	these failures stem from low-level, hardware-specific
59	misuses (e.g., invalid API invocations and memory lay-
60	out mismatches). Moreover, even functionally correct
61	NPU kernels execute nearly 20×slower than their GPU
62	equivalents under identical theoretical compute capacity.
63	Recent efforts to improve NPU kernel generation
64	generally fall into two paradigms: model training (e.g.,
65	domain-adaptive fine-tuning [5] and RL guidance [6])
66	and intermediate representation (IR) assistance (e.g.,
67	lightweight DSLs [7] and polyhedral compilers [8]).

81	Challenge 2: Hardware-Aware Knowledge Re-
82	trieval.Naive retrieval relies functional or textual code
83	similarity, which is fundamentally inadequate for NPU
84	kernels. Two kernels executing identical mathematical
85	operations may require entirely different hardware im-
86	plementations due to distinct memory layouts, tensor
87	shapes, or hardware limits. The challenge lies in design-
88	ing a retrieval mechanism that goes beyond superficial
89	code similarity to accurately capture and match deep
90	hardware-aware constraints.
91	Challenge 3: Context-Aware Knowledge Mainte-
92	nance.Over time, the knowledge base inevitably ac-
93	cumulates erroneous and redundant entries. Erroneous
94	knowledge directly misleads the LLM into generating
95	invalid or crashing kernels. Redundant entries squander
96	the critical context window budget, trapping the LLM
97	in a loop of repeatedly fetching identical strategies. The
98	challenge is to automatically identify and prune this low-
99	quality knowledge based on empirical execution feed-
100	back without disrupting valid contextual dependencies.
101	Hawk incorporates the following three core modules:
102	Run-Time Knowledge Synthesis (Addressing C1).
103	To achieve this synthesis without token exhaustion, this
104	module introduces a Triple-Part Executable Knowledge
105	Representation. Rather than flatly concatenating raw
106	manuals and code, we deconstruct NPU domain knowl-
107	edge into a strict informational hierarchy: (1)indexing
108	triggers(e.g., operator types or data types) for rapid
109	context localization; (2)semantic rationales(e.g., natural
110	language rules regarding NPU Unified Buffer limits or
111	tiling strategies) to explain the underlying hardware con-
112	straints and how to apply the knowledge; and (3)exact
113	syntactic templates(e.g., verified API code snippets)
114	for executable deployment. Crucially, the knowledge is
115	dynamically captured at run-time: whenever the agent
116	meets predefined triggering conditions during kernel
117	generation, it systematically formalizes newly discovered
118	insights into this exact three-part format, ensuring the
119	knowledge base continuously evolves.
120	Bottleneck-Aware Knowledge Retrieval (Address-
121	ing C2).To overcome the limits of naive similarity, this
122	module implements a 2D-Retrieval paradigm. Moving
123	beyond superficial symptom-based text matching, Hawk
124	dynamically projects queries into two orthogonal dimen-
125	sions: a syntactic space ensuring exact API signature
126	compliance, and a hardware-aligned semantic space cap-

payload.delta: \"title\": \"Hawk: Harnessing Hardware-Aware Knowledge for High-Performance NPU Kernel Generation\",\n

\"event_hint\": \"Hawk: a training-free framework that uses hardware-aware knowledge (run-time synthesis, 2D retrieval, effect-driven distillation) to let LLMs generate high-performance Ascend NPU (Ascend C) kernels, targeting the Ascend Da Vinci architecture.\",\n

\"problem\": \"Generating high-performance NPU kernels with LLMs fails because LLMs lack hardware-specific priors: state-of-the-art LLMs achieve only 13.3% Comp@1 and 13.3% Pass@1 on Ascend C (vs 100%/80% on CUDA), over 75% of failures stem from low-level hardware-specific misuses, and even correct NPU kernels run ~20x slower than GPU equivalents under identical theoretical compute capacity.\",\n

\"mechanism\": \"Hawk is a training-free framework with three modules. (1) Run-Time Knowledge Synthesis uses a Triple-Part Executable Knowledge Representation (indexing triggers, semantic rationales, exact syntactic templates) to couple error context with executable semantics, captured dynamically at run time. (2) Bottleneck-Aware Knowledge Retrieval uses a 2D-Retrieval paradigm projecting queries into a syntactic space (API signature compliance) and a hardware-aligned semantic space (memory/parallelization constraints). (3) Effect-Driven Knowledge Distillation uses LLM-driven semantic arbitration with physical NPU compilation/execution feedback to prune erroneous and redundant knowledge entries. Targets the Ascend Da Vinci architecture (AI Cube, AI Vector, multi-tier memory with MTE engines, explicit instruction pipelining).\",\n
\"claim\": \"Hawk elevates NPU kernel generation accuracy from 49.4% to 80.0% and achieves up to 2.2x execution speedup over state-of-the-art baselines on real-world Ascend NPU workloads.\",\n
\"source_locator\": \"Evidence locator: PDF Page 1 - Abstract; PDF Page 11 - Conclusion\"\n

\"claim\": \"SOTA LLMs achieve only 13.3% Comp@1 and 13.3% Pass@1 on Ascend C, vs 100.0% Comp@1 and up to 86.7% Pass@1 on CUDA (DeepSeek-V4 Pro and GLM-4.5, 15 activation kernels from MultiKernelBench, add-shot prompting).\",\n

\"claim\": \"Of 126 classified Ascend C generation failures, 98 (77.8%) are syntax-level (including 53 runtime timeouts, 27 non-existent functions) and 26 (20.6%) are hardware-level (UB overflow); only 2 (1.6%) are numeric correctness mismatches.\",\n
\"claim\": \"Even functionally correct Ascend C kernels execute nearly 20x slower than their GPU equivalents under identical theoretical compute capacity.\",\n

\"claim\": \"Sample timing on RTX 4090D and Ascend 910B2 shows Ascend C kernels far slower than CUDA (e.g., diagonal op: CUDA 0.2ms vs Ascend 37.4ms, 295.6x normalized slowdown; ~22x slower vs PyTorch NPU baseline).\",\n

\"evaluation_context\": \"Evaluated on real-world Ascend NPU workloads (Ascend C kernels). LLMs tested: DeepSeek-V4 Pro and GLM-4.5 (plus supplementary DeepSeek-V4-Flash). Hardware platforms: RTX 4090D and Ascend 910B2. Benchmark: MultiKernelBench, 15 activation kernels (L1/L2 coverage). Knowledge base covers 431 kernels across 8 development-paradigm dimensions. Baselines include fine-tuning (AscendKernelGen, EvoKernel) and IR-assisted frameworks (AKG, AscendCraft, STARK, CudaForge, AVO).\",\n

\"limitations\": \"Test suite covers L1 and L2 kernels; scaling to highly complex fused operators on advanced NPU clusters is left as future work. The 49.4% baseline-accuracy figure is stated without specifying which baseline framework produced it in the visible evidence. Speedup is reported as 'up to 2.2x' (best case); distribution across operator types is not fully exposed. Generalization beyond Ascend (Da Vinci/CANN) is claimed for Ascend 310/950 but not separately measured in the visible evidence.\",\n

\"project_relevance\": \"Hawk is a software/compiler-tooling contribution (NPU kernel generation via LLM + hardware-aware knowledge) rather than a new chip architecture; it is relevant to HW/SW codesign and the memory-IO codesign direction because it targets the Ascend memory hierarchy (Unified Buffer, L0/L1, MTE engines) and exposes how implicit hardware constraints dominate kernel performance. For the project card it addresses the software side of converting NPU peak compute into real throughput, not a silicon or packaging change.\",\n
\"arXiv preprint 2607.01590v2 (2 Jul 2026), FETCHED primary source; authors from Sun Yat-sen University, GBA National Tech Innovation Center, Peng Cheng Laboratory.\",\n
\"Targets Ascend NPU (Da Vinci architecture, CANN toolchain); hardware platforms RTX 4090D and Ascend 910B2.\",\n
\"The 49.4% baseline and 80.0% Hawk accuracy are consistently reported; the specific SOTA baseline behind 49.4% is not named in the visible evidence.\"\n

6	# Technical Briefing Skill
7	
8	## 目标
9	
10	把大量分散、重复、深浅不一的公开技术信息压缩为可信、可读、可追溯并能直接支持项目判断的内部技术简报。
11	
12	默认受众是公司内部领导和技术同事。代码保留4～6条的紧凑模式；当前项目启用`expanded_v2`。每个深度专题最多保留4条完整解读，Top4之外已判定相关且具有A级原始来源的内容进入“专题补充”，每条只保留1～2句总结和原文链接。数量不足时必须少发，不得用弱信息凑数。每2～3天发送一次，不强制覆盖全部专题。

15	
16	- Python负责确定性工作：当前采集、可恢复外部历史回填、过滤、去重、状态、预算、滚动专题池、保守的跨期relevance cache、多样性选择、Evidence Pack、定向Evidence Repair、跨期facts cache、事实任务会话分组、任务成本统计、渲染、邮件和归档。邮件默认通过本机已授权的`agently-cli`发送，SMTP仅作为显式备用后端。
17	- 当前Agent负责智能工作：未命中relevance cache时的批量相关性与价值判断、未命中facts cache时的事实抽取、必要时一次定向facts修复、批量条目草稿写作、一期一次的中文条目润色、按字符预算合并的批量事实校验、综合判断和一期一次的`illustrated_publication`。条目草稿阶段不加载写作Skill；全部草稿完成后`item_style_polish`对整期条目只调用一次`$human-writing`，随后Fact Check验证润色后的最终条目文本。Codex宿主直接使用自身生图能力；Claude Code宿主在该任务中通过已安装的`openai/codex-plugin-cc`把整期生图委派给`codex:codex-rescue`子Agent。兼容的事实抽取可以复用同一Agent会话，但每篇来源的任务、Evidence Pack、输出、Schema、cache和repair始终独立。外部历史分页、游标、时间截断和历史去重不属于Agent任务。
18	- 重点专题走深度通道；Top4之外的相关A级内容走专题补充；AI Infra、Agent生态、KVCache生态、存储与介质等广度信息走Radar通道。
19	- 同一GitHub项目在专题补充中的多条低价值release可以聚合显示，但不得把不同论文或Top4深度条目强行合并。
20	- 不得在Python中绑定某家模型API。
21	- 不得依赖聊天上下文记住历史；常规状态、relevance cache与使用记录写入SQLite，外部历史回填游标写入SQLite `source_state`，回填报告写入被忽略的`workspace/backfill/`，跨期facts写入本地`workspace/cache/facts/`。

66	## 正常运行
67	
68	### 第一步：启动或继续
69	
70	新一轮：
71	
72	```bash
73	python briefing.py run
74	```
75	
76	继续上一轮：
77	
78	```bash
79	python briefing.py resume --run latest
80	```
81	
82	`run`内部调用`collect`。当历史回填尚未完成时，每次正常`collect`只允许使用`historical_backfill.auto_requests_per_collect`规定的小预算推进游标；回填记录先进入独立历史池，不直接创建Agent任务。
83	
84	### 第二步：处理Agent任务
85	
86	运行：
87	
88	```bash
89	python briefing.py tasks next --run latest
90	```
91	
92	严格按命令返回的执行说明处理，不得自行扩大读取范围。普通任务仍是单任务执行；当下一个任务属于`fact_extraction`且存在同专题、同方向、同项目判断卡、同Prompt/Schema的兼容任务时，命令可以返回一个**事实抽取会话组**，默认最多2个独立任务。
93	
94	单任务执行规则：
95	
96	1. 读取指定Prompt；
97	2. 读取指定输入JSON；
98	3. 只读取输入中明确引用的专题判断卡和文档。对于`relevance_batch`，只读取紧凑topic卡、批次级direction卡、候选元数据/摘要和项目判断卡，不主动打开全文；对于`fact_extraction`，正常路径只能读取任务引用的Evidence Pack；对于`fact_evidence_repair`，只能读取结构化旧facts和任务引用的targeted supplement。不得为了“更完整”主动打开未引用的原始全文；
99	4. 输出符合指定Schema的JSON；
100	5. 写入指定输出路径，然后执行`python briefing.py advance --run latest`。
101	
102	事实抽取会话组必须遵守更严格的隔离规则：共享Prompt、Facts Schema和项目判断卡只读取一次；之后严格按命令列出的顺序逐任务处理。每个任务必须单独读取自己的输入JSON和自己的完整Evidence Pack，前一个任务的证据对后一个任务不可采信，不得跨来源比较、归纳、补事实或移动数字；每个任务复制自己的`_task`绑定并写入自己的输出JSON，禁止产生合并数组或batch输出。全部组内输出写完后只执行一次`advance`。会话分组只减少Agent启动和重复上下文加载，不允许减少候选数、Evidence字符、facts字段、Schema校验、语义校验、facts cache、Evidence Repair或后续fact check。
103	
104	需要调试、恢复旧宿主行为，或对会话隔离有任何不确定时，使用：
105	
106	```bash
107	python briefing.py tasks next-single --run latest
108	```
109	
110	它强制只返回一个任务；宁可退化为更多Agent启动，也不得为了分组而截断Evidence或放宽质量门禁。
111	
112	relevance cache命中时，Python会在任务创建前直接恢复`relevant / score / reason / fulltext_required`，因此该候选不再出现在Agent relevance任务中。facts cache命中时，Python会直接复用已验证facts并把候选推进到`FACTS_READY`，不得再启动无意义的事实抽取Agent任务。
113	
114	重复直到运行阶段为`READY_FOR_RENDER`。
115	
116	### 第三步：渲染与审核
117	
118	```bash
119	python briefing.py render --execute
120	python briefing.py validate
121	python briefing.py review --serve
122	```
123	
124	必须先审核再发送。第一版不得自动发送。
125	
126	### 第四步：发送
127	
128	完成审核、修复所有FAIL后：
129	
130	```bash
131	python briefing.py approve --all   # 仅在已人工确认全部条目时使用
132	python briefing.py send --confirm-send
133	```
134	
135	没有`--confirm-send`时必须拒绝发送。使用默认`agently-cli`时，第一次带`--confirm-send`的调用只请求发送确认令牌并停止；将摘要展示给用户，等待用户确认后，再次运行同一命令完成发送。令牌保存在当前运行目录的被忽略文件中，不能提交到仓库。
136	
137	如果需要使用SMTP备用后端，先设置`EMAIL_BACKEND=smtp`，再按同一人工审核和`--confirm-send`门禁发送。

139	## 上下文与成本硬规则
140	
141	1. 禁止一次加载全部搜索结果。
142	2. 规则匹配只负责“找得到”，不能直接代表“值得深读”；Agent在规则过滤前不读取全文。
143	3. A级深度候选按专题批量做价值判断；`max_relevance_batch`默认最多24条，同时受`relevance_batch_max_input_chars`默认48k字符预算约束。topic信息只在批次级出现一次，direction配置必须去重后由候选通过`direction_id`引用；超长摘要默认最多暴露5k字符的完整句摘录。输出仍必须逐候选返回且不得缺失、重复或出现未知ID。只有明确版本arXiv、GitHub Release/Tag、DOI等强版本来源才允许跨期复用relevance；缓存键必须同时匹配来源指纹、topic、direction、Prompt/Schema/项目判断卡形成的evaluator版本和新鲜度区间。普通可变网页不得零评审复用；跨越配置的2/7/30/60天新鲜度边界必须重新评审。不得仅因关键词、topic hint或direction hint自动进入全文分析。
144	4. 只有已解析、非`discovery_only`的A级原始来源才能竞争深度Top4；B/C级和聚合线索进入Radar并继续用于发现原始来源。
145	5. 开放Web搜索只补充A级覆盖缺口，默认每期最多4次。TPN同一方向只有一个项目时仍视为覆盖不足，避免单一项目阻止多样化搜索。
146	6. 深度事实抽取默认每期最多16条、单专题最多4条、同专题同项目最多1条、同方向优先最多2条。其余相关A级候选进入专题补充，不做全文写作和事实检查。
147	7. 原始全文可以在本地保留到`max_fulltext_chars`用于审计，但正常`fact_extraction`默认只读取`evidence_pack_max_chars`控制的Evidence Pack。Evidence Pack必须优先覆盖架构/方法/实验/结果/边界和专题相关段落，并保留章节或页码定位。
148	8. Evidence Pack信息不足时，宁可少写结论并在`limitations`记录缺失验证，也不得自行读取未引用全文或猜测数字。只有当缺失baseline、工作负载/硬件条件、部署边界或明确limitation会实质改变结论解释时，才允许在`evidence_gaps`中提出最多3个具体缺口，并给出可在原文中直接检索的source-native术语。
149	9. 每篇来源最多只允许一轮`fact_evidence_repair`。Python只能在首轮Evidence Pack未曝光的章节中按明确gap terms生成`evidence_repair_max_chars`限制的targeted supplement；repair Agent只读取结构化旧facts和这份supplement。没有明确术语命中时保持保守结论，不得退化为全文搜索；repair后仍缺失的信息保留在`limitations/evidence_gaps`，不得发起第二轮。
150	10. facts cache只能复用稳定来源指纹与运行时抽取版本完全匹配的结果。零抓取复用仅用于明确版本arXiv、GitHub Release/Tag和DOI类强版本身份；普通可变网页必须重新验证。事实Prompt、Facts Schema和Evidence Repair Prompt变化会自动影响运行时版本；Evidence Pack算法发生实质改变时仍应更新`fact_extractor_version`。
151	11. facts cache命中必须走同步fast path，不能再次生成需要Agent处理的事实抽取任务；存在未解决`evidence_gaps`的facts不得写入跨期cache。未命中cache的独立`fact_extraction`任务允许在**不修改任务图和证据量**的前提下复用执行会话：仅同topic+direction+项目判断卡+Prompt/Schema可分组，默认最多2篇且组内Evidence合计默认不超过40k字符；Evidence长度未知、超过预算、不兼容或任何隔离条件无法证明时必须单独运行。分组不得改变任何单篇输出、校验、cache、repair或fact check语义。
152	12. 新运行的深度条目先使用最多4条的`item_writing_batch`独立形成事实受约束的草稿；所有草稿完成后只创建一个`item_style_polish`，对整期条目调用一次`$human-writing`。Fact Check只在该润色任务APPLIED后创建，并优先按`editorial_batch_max_input_chars`字符预算合并；`fact_check_batch_size`默认24只是安全上限，正常一期目标为1～2个`fact_check_batch`。每个event/item仍保持独立ID、来源、Schema/语义校验、provenance和PASS/FAIL，禁止跨条目移动事实。旧run已经存在单条`item_writing`或已有fact-check任务时按旧任务继续恢复。
153	13. `item_writing_batch`不调用任何写作Skill；`item_style_polish`只允许修改标题和五个正文域，不得改变事实、数字、条件、因果强度、ID、score、日期、关键词或来源，并且只加载`$human-writing`一次。Fact Check检查的必须是这份润色后的最终条目文本。`issue_synthesis`直接依据已通过Fact Check的核心条目生成综合判断，不再追加写作Skill，避免事实检查之后再次发生措辞漂移。
154	14. 专题补充默认每专题最多8条、同项目最多2条；每条仅1～2句总结和原文链接，不参与本期综合判断。同一GitHub项目多条低优先级release可聚合为Release Family，必须保留每个原始链接。
155	15. 完成facts抽取/必要的repair后，后续任务只读取结构化facts，不再读取全文。
156	16. 最终综合判断只读取通过事实检查的核心深度解读，不读取专题补充和热点Radar。
157	17. 不要为了“记住上次推送”使用对话记忆；查询SQLite、事件历史、缓存和推送历史。
158	18. 外部历史回填必须是确定性、可分页、可时间截断的Python工作，禁止为“补60天历史”批量创建Agent搜索任务。当前可验证回填只包括arXiv专题方向和配置的GitHub Releases仓库；其他A级源必须显示为`unsupported_sources`，RSS不得假装是完整历史档案。
159	19. 历史回填本身必须产生0个Agent任务。抓取结果写入不属于正常`runs`表的独立历史批次；后续正常run通过`backlog_materialize_per_run`逐步搬入，默认每次最多120条，然后才进入批量价值判断。因此一次回填发现1000条，也不得直接制造1000条Agent任务。
160	20. 每次正常`collect`最多消耗`historical_backfill.auto_requests_per_collect`个历史外部请求，默认4个；不同GitHub/arXiv lane必须公平轮转并持久化游标。手工`backfill --max-requests N`只允许加速同一游标状态，不得绕过去重和下游120条入口预算。
161	
162	成本配置位于`config/settings.yaml`的`efficiency`段。正式运行后优先执行：
163	
164	```bash
165	python briefing.py stats --run latest
166	python briefing.py backfill-status
167	```
168	
169	`stats`检查每种Agent任务的任务数、尝试次数、INVALID次数、facts cache命中、relevance cache条目/本期命中、输入/输出字符量、原始document字符量、Evidence字符量和压缩比例，并额外给出`fact_session_plan`，区分“独立事实任务数”和“预计需要启动的Agent会话数”。`fact_session_plan`只描述调度层复用，不得被解释成少处理了事实任务或少读了证据。`backfill-status`检查历史lane的游标、请求次数、已抓取数量、最老已看到时间、错误、支持/不支持来源。`agent_read_chars_proxy`只是确定性的字符量代理，不是Codex或API真实Token账单；若宿主以后能提供真实usage，必须把真实Token作为首要指标，同时保留字符量用于可复现实验。
170	
171	还可执行：
172	
173	```bash
174	python scripts/estimate_efficiency.py
175	```
176	
177	查看代表性Agent任务数量估算。60天滚动池会增加首次运行的候选数量，但相关性仍按受字符预算约束的批处理；稳定版本来源在评分上下文和新鲜度区间未变化时可跨期复用relevance。专题补充不触发全文、写作和事实检查。任何任务数量或会话数量估算都不等同于实际Token账单，正式运行仍需结合`stats`、人工修改量、端到端耗时和订阅额度。

179	## 时间窗与跨期覆盖
180	
181	- 深度专题使用最近60天的滚动窗口，而不是3天新闻窗口；
182	- arXiv各深度方向与配置的GitHub Release仓库通过持久化游标主动向过去翻页，直到越过本次60天campaign cutoff或来源耗尽；
183	- 外部历史记录先进入独立历史池；每次正常运行再把SQLite中最近60天、尚未推送的A级原始来源按预算带入当前候选池；
184	- `COMPLETE`只表示所有“支持确定性历史分页”的lane已经越过时间边界或耗尽，不得推断`unsupported_sources`也具有完整60天历史；
185	- 已经作为深度条目、专题补充或Radar发送过的稳定身份不得重复出现；
186	- relevance cache不得阻止内容变老：跨越新鲜度评分边界后必须重新评审；
187	- 新鲜度仅占价值判断的小权重，强相关的30～60天内容可以高于当天的弱更新；
188	- 横向热点Radar仍保持最近7天，维持其“快速发现”的定位；
189	- 搜索发现时间和抓取时间不得代替原始发布日期；
190	- 旧事件只有存在明确`incremental_update`及新增内容时才允许重新推送。

192	## 信息源规则
193	
194	### AI HOT
195	
196	AI HOT对以下方向提高优先级：
197	
198	- Agent语义加速；
199	- Coding Agent、CodeGraph、仓库索引和工具链；
200	- KVCache、Prefill/Decode、LLM Serving和Token性能网络；
201	- AI芯片、加速器架构、Chiplet、先进封装和内存接口；
202	- 跨域KVCache和Agent Cache。
203	
204	但AI HOT永远是发现源：
205	
206	```text
207	AI HOT候选
208	→ links.original
209	→ 原始论文/官方博客/仓库
210	→ relevance判断/可验证缓存复用
211	→ Evidence Pack / facts cache
212	→ 事实抽取 / 必要时一次Evidence Repair / 缓存复用
213	```
214	
215	不得把AI HOT的AI摘要直接当作技术证据。
216	
217	### Follow Builders与YeeKal AI Daily
218	
219	Follow Builders用于发现Builder观点、工程实践、访谈和官方博客线索；YeeKal AI Daily用于发现日报中的外部技术文章、项目和社区讨论。两者均保持B级、`discovery_only`，必须回到A级原始论文、官方文档、官方博客或项目仓库后才能进入重点信息。YeeKal日报日期只表示发现时间，不得冒充外部原始发布日期。
220	
221	条目写作采用“批量草稿 → 整期中文润色 → Fact Check”的顺序：`item_writing_batch`只依据各自结构化facts形成草稿；所有草稿完成后，`item_style_polish`把整期条目放在同一个上下文中，只调用一次`$human-writing`消除跨条目的机械句式和机构腔；随后Fact Check逐条独立验证润色后的文字。`issue_synthesis`不再额外调用写作Skill。任何润色都不得增加事实、数字、因果关系或来源。
222	
223	本地未安装`human-writing`时执行：
224	
225	```bash
226	npx skills add https://github.com/KKKKhazix/human-writing --global --agent codex
227	```

229	### 来源等级
230	
231	- A：原始论文、官方文档、官方博客、原项目仓库、正式会议页。
232	- B：高质量聚合、专家分析、作者访谈、独立实践博客。
233	- C：媒体、自媒体、社区和社交平台线索。
234	
235	重点信息至少需要一个已解析A级来源。

237	## 专题与横向Radar
238	
239	深度专题包括：
240	
241	1. 状态感知网络、阿里云Token Performance Network；
242	2. 内存语义、CXL、Intel DSA/IAA卸载；
243	3. DPU/SmartNIC/IPU随路卸载；
244	4. AI芯片与加速器，包括GPU/NPU/TPU/ASIC、Chiplet、先进封装、内存接口和软硬件协同；
245	5. Agent语义加速，包括CodeGraph、Read/Grep/Glob、上下文构建和工具执行链；
246	6. KVCache、Agent Cache和记忆的跨域传输；
247	7. AI/GPU集群光交换网络。
248	
249	基础专题定义在`config/topics.yaml`，AI芯片与加速器定义在`config/topics-chip.yaml`，运行时合并成七个深度专题和一个横向专题。
250	
251	每个深度专题采用两层输出：
252	
253	- **深度Top4**：优先覆盖不同项目和不同技术方向，保留完整机制、证据、边界和项目启发；
254	- **专题补充**：Top4之外仍然相关的A级内容，只给1～2句总结与原文链接。兼容性、例行release等内容更适合放在这里，不应抢占深度Top4。同一GitHub项目的多条普通release可折成一个Release Family，原始链接不能丢。
255	
256	横向Radar保持以下四类召回：
257	
258	- AI Infra：LLM Serving、推理引擎、GPU集群、集合通信、编译器、Kernel、分布式训练、可观测性和故障恢复；
259	- Agent生态：MCP、Computer Use、Browser Agent、Agent Memory、多Agent和开发工具；
260	- KVCache生态：Prefix Cache、量化、分层、路由、持久化以及LMCache、vLLM、SGLang等项目动态；
261	- 存储与介质：HBM、HBF、CXL内存、Persistent Memory、NVMe SSD、NAND、QLC/TLC、ZNS、HDD和Computational Storage。
262	
263	横向强信号只有在拥有A级原始来源、具体机制、量化证据或部署信息并与项目直接相关时，才允许晋升深度通道。具体方向和查询不得在Prompt中重新发明，读取专题配置和对应的`config/project-context/`判断卡。
264	
265	## 相关性与价值判断
266	
267	规则匹配分数只由关键词、query overlap、topic/direction hint和来源优先级组成，用于召回和路由，不得直接当成技术价值分。
268	
269	A级候选进入批量价值判断后，`score`按以下维度形成：
270	
271	- 项目相关性35分；
272	- 技术新颖性/实质机制25分；
273	- 证据具体性20分；
274	- 可行动性15分；
275	- 新鲜度5分。
276	
277	例行兼容、依赖升级、普通bug fix、文档、CI/build和版本号更新可以判为“相关”，但没有实质能力、性能、架构或部署变化时通常不得进入全文Top4，应进入专题补充。最终深读选择还要执行同项目和同方向多样性约束。
278	
279	relevance复用的目标是避免60天滚动池中同一个不可变版本反复支付Agent判断成本，而不是永久冻结评分。只有强版本来源才能缓存；来源版本/内容指纹、Prompt、Schema、当前专题或方向判断上下文、项目判断卡发生变化都会自动miss。由于价值分包含5分新鲜度，缓存还按`freshness_days`边界分桶，跨桶必须重新判断。
280	
281	## 单条信息规则
282	
283	输出应让读者无需打开原文就能理解基本技术方案。内容包括：
284	
285	- 标题；
286	- 类型、专题、日期和重要度；
287	- 一句话核心结论；
288	- 最小必要机制；
289	- 1～2个关键结果及条件；
290	- 最重要的适用边界；
291	- 一个项目启发或下一步验证动作；
292	- 3～5个关键词；
293	- 原始来源。
294	
295	禁止：营销语言、无条件放大预印本结论、遗漏关键基线、把项目推断写成原文事实、以省略号或悬空标点结束字段。五个正文域合计必须为180～260字；优先删除次要背景，不得依赖冒号串联或括号堆叠强行压缩。渲染器不得截断事实检查后的正文。

297	## 跨期去重与热点Radar
298	
299	- 事件身份依次使用arXiv基础ID（忽略`vN`）、DOI、GitHub仓库与Release、规范化原始URL；仅在没有稳定标识时使用语义事件名；

352	
353	- Codex宿主只有在直接生图真实失败时才降级；Claude Code宿主必须先走`openai/codex-plugin-cc`桥接，只有桥接/委派真实失败或图片无法可靠生成时，才把该图标记`fallback_to_text`/`failed`或省略；

355	- 全文抓取失败：使用摘要做低置信Radar候选，但不得成为无A级来源的重点信息。
356	- relevance cache来源指纹、版本、评分上下文或新鲜度桶不匹配：按cache miss重新进入批量价值判断，不得为了省Token强行复用；普通可变网页始终按miss处理。

361	- 邮件失败：不写`last_pushed_at`，下次只重试发送。
362	- 任何配图失败都不能阻塞简报正文。

3	Process one source. Read source metadata, the short topic context, and **only** the Evidence Pack referenced by `document.text_path` / `document.chunks`. The normal Evidence Pack is the beginning of the primary source (roughly abstract + introduction + early design context), not a claim that later evaluation sections were reviewed. Do not open unreferenced raw full text, compare unrelated candidates, or guess missing facts. Copy the input `_task` unchanged to the top level of the output. `title` must exactly match the input source title.

9	- `mechanism`: distinguishing design/mechanism.

11	- `evaluation_context`: workload, scale, hardware/software, baseline, or deployment context that is actually visible.
12	- `limitations`: explicit limits and clearly labelled missing validation.
13	- `project_relevance`: project inference, separate from source facts.

Each gap needs a concrete `question` and 1-8 source-native literal `terms` (system/baseline/hardware/metric/table/workload names) for deterministic retrieval. 2	
3	## 当前关注的问题
4	
5	- 介质侧的容量密度、带宽、时延、耐久、功耗和成本变化，是否足以改变现有存储层级或设备形态？
6	- HBF、QLC/PLC、新型非易失存储或HAMR等方向，哪些已经从器件指标进入系统可用阶段？
7	- 介质创新的收益在控制器、接口、软件栈和真实工作负载下还能保留多少？
8	
9	## 值得进入本期判断的证据
10	
11	优先保留能够回答“介质参数如何转化成系统价值”的证据：量产/原型节点、容量与密度、顺序/随机带宽、访问时延、P/E耐久、写放大、功耗、成本/bit，以及与现有NAND/HDD/DRAM层级的明确对照。单纯材料机理、没有器件或系统量化结果的工作通常只作为观察信号。
12	
13	## 判断边界
14	
15	- HBM及其封装/带宽问题优先归入AI芯片与加速器专题，除非工作核心是非易失介质替代。
16	- CXL内存池化、共享语义和远程访问优先归入内存语义专题。
17	- DPU、NVMe-oF、协议卸载等数据路径优化不因使用SSD而归入介质专题。
18	- 厂商路线图必须区分宣布、送样、量产和规模部署，不能把规划指标写成已实现能力。

39	▲ SK hynix announced on August 4 that it has unveiled the first standard specification for High Bandwidth Flash (HBF), a next-generation storage technology, in collaboration with Sandisk through the OCP.
40	
41	Seoul, August 4, 2026 – SK hynix Inc. (or “the company”, www.skhynix.com ) announced today in collaboration with Sandisk that it has unveiled the first standard specifications for High Bandwidth Flash (HBF), a next-generation storage technology.
42	
43	The announcement coincides with the opening of ‘FMS (Future of Memory and Storage) 2026,’ held at the Santa Clara Convention Center in California from August 4 to 6 (local time). The company is set to present HBF as a key technology to overcome memory bottlenecks in the AI era through keynote speeches and panel discussions during the event.
44	
45	HBF technology is a new memory layer between HBM and SSDs. It enables high-speed data transfer similar to HBM while significantly expanding capacity by leveraging NAND technology. With the expansion of AI inference driving a surge in data volumes to process, HBF is gaining attention as a technology that simultaneously resolves bandwidth and capacity scalability challenges.
46	
47	This milestone comes about six months after launching the consortium in February this year, following the initial standardization partnership with Sandisk in August 2025. Capacity specifications cover up to 512GB based on two stack configurations (8-high and 16-high NAND dies). Bandwidth is categorized into three grades (Grade1~3), delivering scalable performance from approximately 0.4TB/s to 3.0TB/s.
48	
49	A key highlight is the interconnect linking HBF technology and processors. HBF technology adopts UCIe * , an industry standard connection interface, laying the groundwork to flexibly integrate HBF technology across different processor types, including GPUs and CPUs.
50	
51	The standard also outlines ▲connection interfaces and electrical characteristics, ▲reliability and packaging guidelines for HBF die stack process, ▲software I/O guidelines.
52	
53	The specification was disclosed through the Open Compute Project (OCP), world’s largest open data center technology initiative, positioning it as an open standard for the entire industry rather than a proprietary technology.
54	
55	SK hynix plans to leverage this release to expand the adoption of HBF technology in the AI storage market and foster the surrounding ecosystem. With Google and Tenstorrent currently participating in the HBF consortium, the consortium aims to expand its reach while enhancing technical maturity and market acceptance based on open collaboration.

245	LLM inferences are challenges because they involve two phases that use re-
246	sources in different ways: prefill and decode. During the prefill, the input prompt
247	is processed in parallel, which is compute-intensive and effectively utilizes the
248	GPU’s processing power to generate the first token. Then, successive tokens
249	are generated sequentially in auto-regressive fashion in decode steps. To avoid
250	recomputations associated with the attention mechanism (which captures cor-
251	relations between pairs of tokens, most of which do not change between decode
252	steps), a KV cache [16] is often employed to store the K and V vectors (reusable
253	intermediate attention results) of previously computed tokens. The KV cache
254	typically resides in the spare GPU memory not occupied by the model parame-
255	ters. The same principle can be applied across different inference requests that
256	share the same prefix. In this case, the K and V vectors of the longest common
257	prefix can be reused to accelerate the prefill by avoiding redundant attention
258	computations.
259	Limitations of state of art.Modern inference runtimes such as vLLM [10]
260	employ sophisticated KV cache techniques that allow non-contiguous alloca-
261	tion of blocks of GPU memory where the KV results of multiple requests that
262	are batched together and processed in parallel can be stored. To enable prefix
263	caching, a simple approach is to keep KV blocks in the KV cache for as long as
264	possible, subject to an eviction policy (e.g., apply LRU to KV blocks of requests
265	that finished). Then, if a new request arrives that shares a common prefix with
266	a previous request (either finished and not evicted yet or in progress), the blocks
267	corresponding to the longest common prefix can simply be reused (and marked
268	as such by increasing a reference counter). More sophisticated extensions to this
269	technique can be adopted where KV blocks are proactively flushed from GPUs
270	to the host memory (shared by all GPUs on the same compute node), which
271	extends the KV cache capacity of the individual GPUs and allows the reuse of
272	prefixes across requests served by different GPUs, at the expense of slower access.
273	Such an approach is implemented by runtimes such as LMCache [11]. However,
274	at scale, inference requests are served by a large number of GPUs distributed
275	over a large number of compute nodes. In this case, prefixes corresponding to
276	requests served by the GPUs on some nodes can be reused by the GPUs on other
277	nodes.

13	Accelerator for LLM Mixture of Experts 
14	 
15	Pratyush Dhingra, Graduate Student Member, IEEE, Pramit Kumar Pal, Graduate Student Member, IEEE,  
16	Janardhan Rao Doppa, Senior Member, IEEE, and Partha Pratim Pande, Fellow, IEEE

18	 
19	   Abstract—Mixture of Experts (MoE) architectures have 
20	emerged as a dominant paradigm for scaling Large Language 
21	Models (LLMs) . However, MoE inference on conventional 
22	hardware is constrained by three fundamental bottlenecks. These 
23	encompass the massive memory bandwidth required to fetch non-
24	contiguous expert weights, the non -deterministic scatter -gather 
25	traffic generated by input -dependent token routing, and the tail -
26	latency dependency imposed by synchronous expert output 
27	aggregation. To address these challenges, we propose ThAME, a 
28	three-dimensional (3D) heterogeneous multi -chiplet architecture 
29	for MoE inference. ThAME employs Ferroelectric Field -Effect 
30	Transistor (FeFET)-based non-volatile and DRAM-based volatile 
31	memory chiplets with a co -designed compute mapping strategy 
32	that aligns the distinct computational profiles of attention 
33	mechanisms and expert routing . Furthermore, we design a 
34	specialized Network-on-Chip communication backbone optimized 
35	to mitigate the bottlenecks associated with non-deterministic token 
36	routing traffic across the combinatorial space of input -dependent 
37	MoE traffic patterns . Experimental results demonstrate that 
38	ThAME outperforms state-of-the-art counterparts by up to 15.7× 
39	in terms of speedup and improves energy efficiency by up to 9.8×.

44	I. INTRODUCTION 
45	arge Language Models (LLMs) have become a 
46	foundational paradigm in modern AI, delivering  state-
47	of-the-art performance across diverse applications 
48	including language, code, vision, and robotics [1]. Built on the 
49	transformer architecture, they leverage self -attention 
50	mechanisms to capture long -range dependencies  and achieve 
51	exceptional accuracy and generalization capabilities  [1].  
52	Recently, the Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture is rapidly 
53	 
54	 
55	 
56	becoming the preferred practical paradigm to efficiently scale 
57	these models to billions of parameters [2]. By activating a small 
58	subset of specialized experts per token, MoE -based LLMs 
59	achieve high representational power of dense feed -forward 
60	networks through sparse computation [2]. 
61	However, this sparse computation in MoE -based LLM 
62	inference poses significant challenges. First, MoE models 
63	demand enormous memory capacity to store the vast number of 
64	static expert weights. During the autoregressive decode phase, 
65	each generated token nece ssitates fetching large, non -
66	contiguous expert weight matrices from memory. This 
67	memory-bound nature saturates the available bandwidth on 
68	conventional computing platforms such as GPUs, leaving 
69	compute units underutilized [3], [4] . Second, the input -
70	dependent nature of MoE execution produces irregular 
71	dataflow.

92	V. EXPERIMENTAL RESULTS 
93	In this section, we first describe the experimental setup used 
94	for the performance evaluation  of ThAME. Next, we analyze 
95	the ThAME compute core design followed by the NoC design 
96	within the FeFET -NAND die . Afterwards, we analyze the 
97	effectiveness of both the computation and communication 
98	optimization during expert processing . We then present a 
99	sensitivity analysis under degraded FeFET read latency. 
100	Finally, we present a comparative and end -to-end analysis of 
101	ThAME against the baselines  in terms of performance and 
102	energy during MoE LLM inference. 
103	A. Experimental Setup 
104	We consider a diverse range of LLM models in our 
105	evaluation, as outlined in Table I . These models represent the 
106	typical size and diversity of real -world use  cases for 
107	deployment. A 16-bit fixed-point data representation was used 
108	as the precision of all model parameters and activations.  
109	Compute Modeling: We employed a cycle-accurate simulator 
110	to determine the latency and energy for each compute unit. 
111	SCALE-Sim was used to model the latency for each systolic 
112	array within the base die of memory chiplets and the host [34]. 
113	For the FeFET -NAND P NM chiplet, a modified version of 
114	NeuroSim was employed to capture the latency and energy of 
115	the 3D memory array [39]. NeuroSim has been validated against 
116	post-layout SPICE simulations of a taped -out PIM macro, 
117	showing chip-level prediction error below 1% after calibration 
118	for area, latency, and energy metrics. Similarly, SCALE-Sim has 
119	been verified against production TPU hardware with median 
120	relative error below 3% for representative operators [34]. Table 
121	II provides the detailed specifications of the FeFET -NAND, 
122	DRAM, and host chiplets used in our evaluation.  
123	Communication Modeling:  BookSim2, a cycle -accurate 
124	simulator, was used to model the  intra-chiplet NoC [40]. The 
125	inputs to the BookSim2 are the connectivity between routers, the 
126	intra-chiplet traffic, the link bandwidth, and the routing 
127	algorithm. Table III shows the NoC parameters for modeling the 
128	inter-core links within the FeFET-NAND chiplet.  
129	In this work, we have implemented ThAME using a 
130	configuration with two FeFET and two DRAM memory chiplets 
131	along with a systolic array (TPU v6e) based host chiplet on a 
132	silicon interposer. Each of the memory chiplets is connected to 
133	the host chiplet in a point -to-point manner through the 
134	interposer. Note that this specific configuration does not affect 
135	the generalizability of our findings.  We compare ThAME 
136	against two heterogeneous accelerators, Stratum (a DRAM -
137	PNM and compute -centric host) and H3D -T (a 3D -stacked 
138	FeFET, SRAM, and TPU architecture)  [9], [15]. The base die 
139	area for both the DRAM and the FeFET -NAND chiplet is kept 
140	consistent at  121 mm 2, simi lar to the baseline Stratum for 
141	comparison. For H3D-T, we instantiat e multiple instances to 
142	establish an iso-area configuration for a fair evaluation. 
143	The base  die within the FeFET -NAND chiplet consists of 
144	systolic array-based computing cores. We follow existing work 
145	to determine the area and power for the memory peripherals, 
146	PHY and the power-delivery network for the base die [15]. To 
147	perform the thermal evaluation and to ensure the feasibility of 
148	the 3D-stacked base die without inducing thermal throttling, we 
149	employed HotSpot [41]. We performed a steady -state 
150	simulation at a 45 C ambient to establish an allowable budget of 
151	50W for the base die, using the parameters detailed in Table III. 
152	Given the area budget and FeFET memory bandwidth in our 
153	experimental setup, we provisioned a total of 4,096 PEs per core 
154	in a 32-core system under maximum utilization where all cores 
155	are simultaneously active. Table IV details the specifications of 
156	the systolic array  cores. We employ the Archived Multi -
157	Objective Simulated Annealing (AMOSA) algorithm to identify 
158	the Pareto-Optimal set of designs (𝒟∗) for our hierarchical NoC 
159	design. AMOSA is a simulated annealing-based MOO solver in 
160	which the optimization process is guided using an archive of 
161	previously explored solutions [38]. The design space exploration

200	In parallel, industry has begun exploring high -bandwidth 
201	NAND with near -memory compute for AI inference. SanDisk

208	While these efforts confirm the practical feasibility of dense 
209	NAND for overcoming DRAM's capacity and refresh 
210	limitations, they rely on conventional Flash, which imposes 
211	high access latency and energy overheads. Moreover, similar to 
212	existing HBM -based PNM systems, they provide no intra -
213	chiplet fabric to manage the irregular, scatter -gather data 
214	exchange among compute cores during MoE token routing. 
215	Collectively, these efforts advance either storage density or 
216	raw bandwidth, yet none couples low -latency, high -density 
217	storage with a communication fabric designed for MoE traffic. 
218	This gap motivates a co -designed architecture that integrates 
219	such storage with a specialized NoC to break both the memory 
220	and communication bottlenecks of MoE inference. 
221	III. PROBLEM STATEMENT 
222	Each layer within a transformer based LLM is composed of 
223	two computational modules: Multi-Head Attention (MHA) and 
224	Feed-Forward (FFN) [1]. While the MHA module remains 
225	consistent across LLMs and MoE models, the structure of the 
226	FFN is fundamentally different between these architectures . In 
227	MoE, the monolithic FFN of LLMs is replaced with a sparse 
228	layer of independent specialized experts (see Fig. 2)  [2], [17]. 
229	Specifically, a MoE layer consists of a Router (or Gating 
230	Network) and a set of 𝑁 independent expert networks 𝐸 =
231	 {𝐸1, … , 𝐸𝑁}, each implemented as a standard FFN, where 
232	computation is inherently sparse, activating only a small subset 
233	of relevant experts per input [2], [17]. 
234	For a given input token representation 𝑥, the gating network  
235	𝐺(𝑥) computes a sparse probability distribution, selecting only 
236	the top-𝑘 experts (where 𝑘 ≪ 𝑁) to process the token, as shown 
237	in Fig. 2 . Afterwards, the output 𝑦 is the weighted sum of the 
238	selected experts' outputs, as described in Eq. 1: 
239	                                  𝑦 =  ∑ 𝐺(𝑥)𝑖. 𝐸𝑖(𝑥)𝑖 ∈𝑇                          (1) 
240	where 𝑇 represents the set of indices corresponding to the 
241	top-𝑘 experts. While this sparsity keeps the number of active 
242	parameters per token comparable to a smaller model, the total 
243	number of model parameters to be stored for all experts can be 
244	orders of magnitude larger. This shift in neural architecture 
245	creates fundamental challenges : MoE models are 
246	computationally sparse but memory -dense, introducing 
247	significant irregularity in dataflow. The workload transitions 
248	from the uniform matrix multiplication  characteristic of LLMs 
249	to scattered, input-dependent conditional computation in MoEs, 
250	creating both computation and communication bottlenecks. 
251	First, t he expert weights dominate the model size (often >  
252	90%). Storing these massive parameters in off -chip Flash 
253	memory incurs prohibitive latency and energy penalties, while 
254	on-chip DRAM lacks the required density. Consequently, 
255	efficient expert computation demands a high -density storage 
256	medium capable of low-latency access. 
257	Second, the active experts are dynamically allocated to the 
258	computing cores. Considering a manycore architecture, the 
259	gating mechanism dictates the workload distribution for a batch 
260	of input tokens. This results in highly variable , non-
261	deterministic traffic patterns that change based on the semantic 
262	content of the batch [12]. Tokens must be dispatched to their 
263	assigned experts and output results aggregated, introducing 
264	significant network latency [13]. Furthermore, the aggregation 
265	of expert outputs imposes a synchronous aggregation operation, 
266	where the inference latency is dictated by the completion of the 
267	slowest expert.  
268	From a combinatorial perspective, the allocation of 𝑞 cores to 
269	𝑒 active experts can be modeled as partitioning the integer 𝑞 
270	into 𝑒 parts. Consequently, the total number of unique NoC 
271	traffic scenarios (𝑆), for a system with 𝑞 cores is given by the 
272	sum of partition functions, as expressed in Eq. 2: 
273	                                       𝑆 =  ∑ 𝑝𝑗(𝑞)
274	𝑒
275	𝑗=1                                   (2) 
276	Here, 𝑝𝑗(𝑞) represents the number of integer partitions of 𝑞 into 
277	exactly 𝑗 positive parts. 
278	This combinatorial explosion of traffic patterns , combined 
279	with the memory-bound nature of experts, impose the following 
280	design challenges unique to MoE-based LLM inference: 
281	1) Memory Bottleneck of Experts:  The expert layers 
282	require massive storage density and high bandwidth to 
283	feed compute units. Existing memory hierarchies fail to 
284	balance the trade-off between density, leakage, and access 
285	latency for these sparse, static weights.

351	VI. CONCLUSION 
352	MoE neural architectures have emerged as a powerful 
353	paradigm for scaling LLMs, but their deployment is 
354	fundamentally bottlenecked by the extreme memory demands 
355	of static expert weights and the non -deterministic 
356	communication traffic due to input -dependent expert routing. 
357	This paper presented ThAME, a three -dimensional 
358	heterogeneous architecture designed to accelerate MoE 
359	inference. By harnessing the high storage density of 3D FeFET-
360	NAND memory for experts, ThAME stores model parameters 
361	on-chip, effectively breaking the memory wall. Furthermor e, 
362	we design a customized hierarchical NoC for the intra -chiplet 
363	traffic within FeFET -NAND. This specialized communication 
364	backbone reduces link utilization variance, mitigating the 
365	multi-hop congestion and tail -latency stalls that cripple 
366	conventional topologies such as mesh during expert processing.

63	Abstract
64	Vision-language-action (VLA) models have emerged as a key com-
65	ponent in embodied AI. Among existing approaches, diffusion-
66	based VLA models achieve superior motion quality and generaliza-
67	tion. However, diffusion-based VLA models are compute-intensive
68	and must run at high control frequency, e.g., 50–200 Hz. Thus, it
69	imposes strict latency and energy constraints on edge devices.
70	In this work, we presentDeltoris 1, an algorithm–hardware
71	co-design framework for efficient diffusion-based VLA inference.
72	First, we exploit the temporal similarity of consecutive inputs and
73	propose atemporal-aware bit-sparsityalgorithm that computes only
74	the differences between consecutive inputs, eliminating redundant
75	bit-level operations. To further address the extra off-chip traffic
76	introduced by our algorithm, we propose aspeculative inference
77	technique, which amortizes data loading across multiple control
78	steps. Lastly, to support these techniques, we co-design a dedicated
79	accelerator with customized 1D systolic bit-serial PE arrays that
80	eliminate PE workload imbalance. Our evaluation shows thatDel-
81	torisachieves up to 34.2 × speedup over mobile GPUs and 6.1 ×
82	over prior accelerators, while maintaining comparable accuracy.

90	1 Introduction
91	Recent advances in embodied artificial intelligence (AI) have en-
92	abled robots to perform complex tasks in real-world environments [1,
93	32, 34, 104, 117]. At the core of these systems are vision-language-
94	action (VLA) models, which integrate visual perception, instruction
95	understanding, and action generation into a unified framework. By
96	leveraging multimodal inputs, VLA models allow robots to interpret
97	high-level instructions and convert them into control commands.

104	compression [8, 19, 35], sparse attention [15, 49, 94], etc. In con-
105	trast, VLA models remain largelyunder-exploredin the architecture
106	community. Currently, enabling VLA models on robotic platforms
107	in real-time is challenging due to their latency and energy con-
108	straints. Existing robotic platforms often fail to meet the real-time
109	requirements (50–200 Hz). For instance, a well-known VLA model,
110	PAD [26], can only execute at 2.0 Hz on a mobile Nvidia Orin
111	SoC (Fig. 2). Thus, this paper aims to enable real-time and energy-
112	efficient VLA model inference on robotic platforms.
113	Among the VLA models [5, 6, 12, 20, 26, 36, 43, 53, 54, 61, 90, 92,
114	96, 105] proposed in recent years, diffusion-based models [5, 12, 20,
115	26, 36, 53, 61, 90, 92] have emerged as a promising approach for
116	robot control. Compared to other inference paradigms, diffusion-
117	based VLA models can produce smooth motion trajectories and
118	achieve better generality among unseen environments by predicting
119	the action distribution through an iterative noise-denoising process.
120	Recent works, such as Diffusion Policy [12], UVA [36], VPP [36], and
121	Diffusion-VLA [90] demonstrate that diffusion-based approaches
122	can outperform traditional auto-regressive (AR) policies in many
123	robotic manipulation benchmarks. In this paper, we primarily focus
124	on diffusion-based VLA models.
125	Motivation.Despite their advantages, diffusion-based VLA
126	models are compute-intensive. They require tens of iterative de-
127	noising steps to generate one individual action, resulting in a higher
128	latency compared to their AR counterparts. Each denoising step
129	involves executing a deep neural network (DNN) to progressively
130	refine a noisy trajectory into a valid control signal. Our roofline anal-
131	ysis in Fig. 5 shows that existing diffusion-based VLA models are
132	compute-bound rather than memory-bound. Thus, it is important
133	to reduce the overall computation of diffusion-based VLA models.
134	To do so, our key insight is that consecutive robot observations,
135	e.g., poses and images, in robotic control loops exhibit extremely
136	high similarity, given the fact that robot control operates at a high
137	frequency. Our experiment in Fig. 7 shows that over 98% of pixels
138	between consecutive camera frames often remain unchanged due to
139	the small time interval between controls. As a result, a large portion
140	of the computation during VLA inference is redundant. Potentially,
141	we can enable orders-of-magnitude speedup for diffusion-based
142	VLA inference by exploiting this temporal redundancy.
143	Framework.To exploit this insight, we proposeDeltoris, an al-
144	gorithm–hardware co-design framework for accelerating diffusion-
145	based VLA models.Deltorisexploits the high temporal similarity
146	inherent in robotic control loops and introduces atemporal-aware
147	bit-level sparsityalgorithm that processes only the differences be-
148	tween consecutive inputs (Sec. 4). Similar to the execution of spiking
149	neural networks [98],Deltorisrepresents differential inputs in bi-
150	nary form and executes computations only on active “1” bits while
151	skipping redundant operations. Our experiment shows in Fig. 17
152	that we can achieve up to 92.9% operation reduction.
153	Although our bit sparsity algorithm significantly reduces arith-
154	metic operations, it introduces additional off-chip data traffic due to
155	the extra intermediate data loading. We show that a naive bit spar-
156	sity implementation can increase the off-chip data traffic by 1.8×.
157	We found that the VLA workloads essentially shift from compute-
158	bound to memory-bound after applying our bit-level sparsity al-
159	gorithm. To mitigate the DRAM traffic overhead, we propose a
160	technique calledspeculative inferencein Sec. 5, inspired by specula-
161	tive decoding in LLMs [50, 63]. In our approach, a lightweight VLA
162	model first speculatively predicts multiple future actions, while a
163	more accurate but compute-intensive VLA model validates these
164	predictions. To maintain robustness, no actions are actually applied
165	to the robots before being validated by the larger VLA model. In this
166	way, both model weights and intermediate data of the larger model
167	can be loaded only once when validating all predicted poses. Thus,
168	our approach amortizes data loading across multiple validation
169	steps, reducing off-chip data traffic.
170	Architecture.To fully unlock the potential ofDeltoris, we
171	design a dedicated accelerator tailored for diffusion-based VLA in-
172	ference in Sec. 6. The key contribution of our design is to eliminate
173	the workload imbalance commonly observed in bit-serial accel-
174	erators that exploit bit-level sparsity. Specifically, we employ an
175	output-stationary dataflow that shares activations across multi-
176	ple processing elements (PEs). We further introduce a novel 1D
177	systolic bit-serial PE array. Compared with prior bit-serial acceler-
178	ators, our proposed PE array largely simplifies control logic and
179	improves both performance and energy efficiency. Combined with
180	our co-designed encoding and decoding modules, our architecture
181	effectively reduces both on-chip and off-chip data movement.

19	Abstract—Developing high-performance kernels for Neu-
20	ral Processing Units (NPUs) is a critical industry bottle-
21	neck, requiring developers to manually navigate implicit
22	hardware constraints and strict memory hierarchies. While
23	large language models offer immense automation potential,
24	they fail catastrophically on NPUs due to a fundamental
25	lack of hardware-specific priors. Na ¨ıvely transplanting
26	code snippets from similar NPU kernels may pass the
27	compiler, but it consistently triggers runtime crashes and
28	performance degradation by blindly violating underlying
29	hardware constraints. To overcome this, we introduce
30	Hawk, a training-free framework that harnesses hardware-
31	aware knowledge through three core modules: (1) Run-
32	Time Knowledge Synthesis Module, which employs a
33	Triple-Part Executable Knowledge Representationto inher-
34	ently couple the error context with executable semantics;
35	(2) Bottleneck-Aware Knowledge Retrieval Module, which
36	implements a2D-Retrievalparadigm to project queries
37	into orthogonal syntactic and hardware-aligned seman-
38	tic spaces; and (3) Effect-Driven Knowledge Distillation
39	Module, which leveragesLLM-driven semantic arbitration
40	to continuously distill the knowledge by pruning errors
41	and consolidating redundancies based on the empirical
42	execution feedback. Extensive evaluations on real-world
43	NPU workloads demonstrate that Hawk elevates generation
44	accuracy from 49.4% to 80.0%, while achieving up to a
45	2.2×execution speedup over state-of-the-art baselines.
46	Index Terms—NPU, Kernel Generation, Harness Engi-
47	neering, Automatic Programming.
48	I. INTRODUCTION
49	Domain-specific accelerators like Neural Processing
50	Units (NPUs) are critical for modern AI workloads, yet
51	automating NPU kernel generation via Large Language
52	Models (LLMs) [1]–[4] remains notoriously difficult.
53	Our empirical study (§III) shows state-of-the-art LLMs
54	achieve merely 13.3% Comp@1 (compilation success
55	rate) and 13.3% Pass@1 (functional correctness rate) on
56	NPUs, starkly contrasting with GPU generation (100%
57	Comp@1, 80% Pass@1). We find that over 75% of
58	these failures stem from low-level, hardware-specific
59	misuses (e.g., invalid API invocations and memory lay-
60	out mismatches). Moreover, even functionally correct
61	NPU kernels execute nearly 20×slower than their GPU
62	equivalents under identical theoretical compute capacity.
63	Recent efforts to improve NPU kernel generation
64	generally fall into two paradigms: model training (e.g.,
65	domain-adaptive fine-tuning [5] and RL guidance [6])
66	and intermediate representation (IR) assistance (e.g.,
67	lightweight DSLs [7] and polyhedral compilers [8]).

82	trieval.Naive retrieval relies functional or textual code

84	kernels. Two kernels executing identical mathematical
85	operations may require entirely different hardware im-
86	plementations due to distinct memory layouts, tensor
87	shapes, or hardware limits. The challenge lies in design-
88	ing a retrieval mechanism that goes beyond superficial
89	code similarity to accurately capture and match deep
90	hardware-aware constraints.
91	Challenge 3: Context-Aware Knowledge Mainte-
92	nance.Over time, the knowledge base inevitably ac-
93	cumulates erroneous and redundant entries. Erroneous
94	knowledge directly misleads the LLM into generating
95	invalid or crashing kernels. Redundant entries squander
96	the critical context window budget, trapping the LLM
97	in a loop of repeatedly fetching identical strategies. The
98	challenge is to automatically identify and prune this low-
99	quality knowledge based on empirical execution feed-
100	back without disrupting valid contextual dependencies.
101	Hawk incorporates the following three core modules:
102	Run-Time Knowledge Synthesis (Addressing C1).
103	To achieve this synthesis without token exhaustion, this
104	module introduces a Triple-Part Executable Knowledge
105	Representation. Rather than flatly concatenating raw
106	manuals and code, we deconstruct NPU domain knowl-
107	edge into a strict informational hierarchy: (1)indexing
108	triggers(e.g., operator types or data types) for rapid
109	context localization; (2)semantic rationales(e.g., natural
110	language rules regarding NPU Unified Buffer limits or
111	tiling strategies) to explain the underlying hardware con-
112	straints and how to apply the knowledge; and (3)exact
113	syntactic templates(e.g., verified API code snippets)
114	for executable deployment. Crucially, the knowledge is
115	dynamically captured at run-time: whenever the agent
116	meets predefined triggering conditions during kernel
117	generation, it systematically formalizes newly discovered
118	insights into this exact three-part format, ensuring the
119	knowledge base continuously evolves.

124	dynamically projects queries into two orthogonal dimen-

126	compliance, and a hardware-aligned semantic space cap-

7	
8	## 目标
9	
10	把大量分散、重复、深浅不一的公开技术信息压缩为可信、可读、可追溯并能直接支持项目判断的内部技术简报。
11	
12	默认受众是公司内部领导和技术同事。代码保留4～6条的紧凑模式；当前项目启用`expanded_v2`。每个深度专题最多保留4条完整解读，Top4之外已判定相关且具有A级原始来源的内容进入“专题补充”，每条只保留1～2句总结和原文链接。数量不足时必须少发，不得用弱信息凑数。每2～3天发送一次，不强制覆盖全部专题。

16	- Python负责确定性工作：当前采集、可恢复外部历史回填、过滤、去重、状态、预算、滚动专题池、保守的跨期relevance cache、多样性选择、Evidence Pack、定向Evidence Repair、跨期facts cache、事实任务会话分组、任务成本统计、渲染、邮件和归档。邮件默认通过本机已授权的`agently-cli`发送，SMTP仅作为显式备用后端。

98	3. 只读取输入中明确引用的专题判断卡和文档。对于`relevance_batch`，只读取紧凑topic卡、批次级direction卡、候选元数据/摘要和项目判断卡，不主动打开全文；对于`fact_extraction`，正常路径只能读取任务引用的Evidence Pack；对于`fact_evidence_repair`，只能读取结构化旧facts和任务引用的targeted supplement。不得为了“更完整”主动打开未引用的原始全文；
99	4. 输出符合指定Schema的JSON；
100	5. 写入指定输出路径，然后执行`python briefing.py advance --run latest`。
101	
102	事实抽取会话组必须遵守更严格的隔离规则：共享Prompt、Facts Schema和项目判断卡只读取一次；之后严格按命令列出的顺序逐任务处理。每个任务必须单独读取自己的输入JSON和自己的完整Evidence Pack，前一个任务的证据对后一个任务不可采信，不得跨来源比较、归纳、补事实或移动数字；每个任务复制自己的`_task`绑定并写入自己的输出JSON，禁止产生合并数组或batch输出。全部组内输出写完后只执行一次`advance`。会话分组只减少Agent启动和重复上下文加载，不允许减少候选数、Evidence字符、facts字段、Schema校验、语义校验、facts cache、Evidence Repair或后续fact check。
103	
104	需要调试、恢复旧宿主行为，或对会话隔离有任何不确定时，使用：
105	
106	```bash
107	python briefing.py tasks next-single --run latest
108	```
109	
110	它强制只返回一个任务；宁可退化为更多Agent启动，也不得为了分组而截断Evidence或放宽质量门禁。
111	
112	relevance cache命中时，Python会在任务创建前直接恢复`relevant / score / reason / fulltext_required`，因此该候选不再出现在Agent relevance任务中。facts cache命中时，Python会直接复用已验证facts并把候选推进到`FACTS_READY`，不得再启动无意义的事实抽取Agent任务。
113	
114	重复直到运行阶段为`READY_FOR_RENDER`。
115	
116	### 第三步：渲染与审核
117	
118	```bash
119	python briefing.py render --execute
120	python briefing.py validate
121	python briefing.py review --serve
122	```
123	
124	必须先审核再发送。第一版不得自动发送。
125	
126	### 第四步：发送
127	
128	完成审核、修复所有FAIL后：
129	
130	```bash
131	python briefing.py approve --all   # 仅在已人工确认全部条目时使用
132	python briefing.py send --confirm-send
133	```
134	
135	没有`--confirm-send`时必须拒绝发送。使用默认`agently-cli`时，第一次带`--confirm-send`的调用只请求发送确认令牌并停止；将摘要展示给用户，等待用户确认后，再次运行同一命令完成发送。令牌保存在当前运行目录的被忽略文件中，不能提交到仓库。
136	
137	如果需要使用SMTP备用后端，先设置`EMAIL_BACKEND=smtp`，再按同一人工审核和`--confirm-send`门禁发送。
